water purification: FIRST: boiling and bleach kill germs but do NOT remove chemicals, fuel, salts or heavy metals. If the water may have those (floodwater, near fields, roads, mines or spills), find another source. CLOUDY WATER: let it settle, then filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter before treating. BOILING (most reliable): a rolling boil for at least 1 minute; above 5,000 feet (about 1,500 m) boil for 3 minutes. Let it cool and store it covered. BLEACH (if you can't boil): only regular, unscented chlorine bleach labeled for disinfection, 6% or 8.25% sodium hypochlorite; never scented, color-safe or bleach with added cleaners. Per 1 liter or quart: 2 drops (6% or 8.25%). Per gallon: 8 drops of 6% or 6 drops of 8.25%. DOUBLE the dose if the water is cloudy, colored or very cold. Stir and wait 30 minutes; it should smell slightly of chlorine. If it doesn't, repeat the dose and wait 15 more minutes. Don't use water with floating material, a dark color or a strange smell. Tablets or iodine: follow the label. Questions: EPA Safe Drinking Water Hotline 1-800-426-4791.
fire starting: Priority: lighter/matches (carry redundant). Ferrocerium rod works wet. Bow drill: dry softwood spindle in dry hardboard, steady downward pressure, tinder bundle ready. Flint and steel: strike at 30 degrees onto char cloth. Tinder materials: dry grass, cattail fluff, birch bark, cedar bark, fatwood shavings. Always prepare tinder bundle completely before attempting ignition.
shelter priorities: Order: insulation from ground first (conduction hypothermia kills fastest). Lean-to: ridge pole between trees, branches at 45 degrees, debris 30cm thick. Debris hut: frame like upturned boat, fill with leaves, 1m thick sides. Desert: shade above, air gap for convection cooling, never on sand at noon. Snow quinzhee: pile snow 2h to sinter, hollow out 10cm walls, poke ventilation hole through top. R-value of dead air space is your goal.
navigation without compass: Sun: rises east, sets west; N hemisphere noon shadow points north. Stars: Polaris is North Star — find Big Dipper outer edge, follow 5x to bright star. Analog watch: point hour hand at sun, bisect angle to 12 = south (N hemisphere). Shadow stick method: mark shadow tip, wait 15 min, second tip, line between = east-west. Follow water downstream leads to human settlement in most temperate regions.
signaling for rescue: Mirror flash visible 16+ km — most effective daytime signal. Three of anything = international distress: 3 whistle blasts, 3 fires in triangle, 3 smoke columns. Ground signals: X = need medical help, V = need help, arrow = direction of travel. Smoke: green rubber/plastic for dark smoke in clear air; damp green grass for white smoke in haze. Cell phone: SMS reaches further than voice; summit/clearing for signal. Whistle carries further than voice at fraction of energy.
food preservation no electricity: DRYING: slice 5mm thin, dry at 55-70C until brittle. SALTING: 10% salt by weight draws moisture via osmosis. LACTO-FERMENTATION: 2% salt by weight, pack tight, anaerobic — sauerkraut, kimchi; lactic acid preserves indefinitely when sealed. SMOKING: cold smoke below 32C for maximum preservation; hot smoke cooks first. CANNING: must reach 121C to kill Clostridium botulinum spores — requires pressure canner. Dried + salted = longest shelf life with no equipment.
rope knots essential: BOWLINE: fixed non-slip loop, rescue standard — rabbit comes out of hole, around tree, back in hole. CLOVE HITCH: tie to post, adjustable, start all lashings. SHEET BEND: join ropes of different diameter. FIGURE EIGHT: stopper and climbing anchor. PRUSIK: ascending fixed rope — use 6mm cord on 10mm. TAUT LINE HITCH: adjustable tension on tent guylines. REEF KNOT: bandages and bags only — NEVER for life safety. Practice each 20 repetitions until automatic.
foraging edibility test: Universal Edibility Test (not for mushrooms — many are acutely lethal): 1) Separate plant parts. 2) Smell: bitter almond or peach-pit odor = reject. 3) Touch small piece to lip 15 min — burning/itching = reject. 4) Chew small piece, hold 15 min in mouth — reject if burns or numbs. 5) Swallow tiny amount, wait 8h — reject if nausea. 6) Eat small handful, wait 8h — proceed if no reaction. Safe known plants: dandelion (all parts), cattail (all parts, all seasons), plantain, chicory.
hypothermia prevention: CLOTHING LAYERS: wicking base (merino/synthetic), insulation (down/fleece), wind/waterproof shell. COTTON KILLS — retains moisture, eliminates insulation when wet. SYMPTOMS: shivering (mild, 35-32C) → confusion/slurred speech (moderate, 32-28C) → no shivering, rigid, unconscious (severe, below 28C). TREATMENT: remove wet clothing, horizontal position, insulate from ground, body-to-body heat transfer, warm sweet liquids if fully conscious. Do not rub extremities — drives cold blood to core.
frostbite treatment: Do NOT rub frozen tissue — crystals shred cells. Do NOT rewarm if refreezing is possible — thaw-refreeze causes worse damage than staying frozen. REWARMING: 40-42C water bath, not hotter, 15-30 min until pink/pliable. Expect intense pain during rewarming (normal). Protect blisters — do not break. Evacuate. Early frostnip (white, waxy, numb skin): rewarm with body heat immediately, no lasting damage if caught early.
rainwater harvesting: COLLECTION MATH: 1mm rainfall on 1m2 = 1 liter. Use non-toxic surfaces only — HDPE plastic, metal (not galvanized with lead), clean tarps. FIRST-FLUSH DIVERTER: discard first 25L per 93m2 of roof to remove bird droppings and dust. STORAGE: covered, dark container prevents algae; dark reduces temperature fluctuation. TREATMENT: boil or filter + disinfect before drinking regardless of apparent cleanliness.
seed saving: Save only from open-pollinated non-hybrid varieties — F1 hybrids do not breed true. Fully dry seeds before storage — snap test: should snap, not bend. Store in paper envelopes inside sealed glass jars with silica gel, cool/dark/dry. VIABILITY BY SPECIES: onion/parsnip 1-2 years; corn/tomato 3-5 years; beans/squash/pumpkin 5-10 years. ISOLATION DISTANCES: corn 400m minimum; brassicas 300m; tomatoes 10m (self-pollinating); peppers 150m.
composting hot method: RATIO: 3:1 carbon:nitrogen by volume. CARBON (brown): dried leaves, cardboard, straw, wood chips. NITROGEN (green): kitchen scraps, fresh grass, manure, coffee grounds. MOISTURE: squeeze test — few drops only. SIZE: minimum 1 cubic meter to generate heat. TURN weekly to maintain 55-65C — this temperature kills pathogens and weed seeds. READY in 3-6 weeks: dark, earthy, crumbly, no recognizable materials. Do NOT add: meat, dairy, diseased plants, treated wood.
basic irrigation: GRAVITY DRIP: 1m elevation head = 0.1 bar pressure — sufficient for drip emitters. Drip uses 50-70% less water than flood irrigation. SWALES: level trenches on contour capture rainwater and allow infiltration — appropriate technology permaculture standard. MULCH: 5-10cm layer reduces water needs 50%, suppresses weeds, builds soil. TIMING: water at dawn — minimizes evaporation (noon = 50% loss to evaporation) and fungal disease. SOIL TEST: finger 5cm deep — water only when dry at that depth.
soil testing field methods: pH: universal indicator strips or red cabbage juice (red = acid, green = alkaline). TEXTURE: jar test — soil plus water, shake, settle 2 days; sand settles first (bottom), silt middle, clay top. DRAINAGE: dig 30cm hole, fill water, time to drain — under 1h fast, 1-4h good, over 8h poor drainage. ORGANIC MATTER: squeeze moist soil — crumbles easily = good; sticky ball = high clay, low OM; falls apart = low clay, sand. TARGET: loamy soil with 5%+ organic matter, pH 6.0-7.0 for most crops.
crop rotation principles: 4-year minimum rotation to break pest and disease cycles. FAMILY GROUPS: brassicas (cabbage, broccoli, kale); nightshades (tomato, potato, pepper); legumes (beans, peas — fix nitrogen); alliums (onion, garlic); roots (carrot, parsnip). SEQUENCE: legumes → brassicas (use nitrogen) → roots → alliums. Never follow brassica with brassica — clubroot persists 20 years. Legumes add 50-200 kg nitrogen/hectare/year when inoculated with correct rhizobia.
food calorie priorities survival: CALORIE DENSITY per 100g: fat 900kcal, nuts 600kcal, dried meat 350kcal, dried grains 340kcal, legumes 340kcal. MACRO PRIORITY SHORT-TERM: animal protein first (complete amino acids + fat), then starches, then vegetables. ENERGY BUDGET: do not expend more calories foraging than food provides. WATER: required for protein/fat metabolism — no food without water first. 3-day fast is survivable; prioritize water (3 days max without) and shelter (hours in cold) before food.
animal tracking basic: TRACK PATTERNS: straddle = left-right distance; stride = same-foot distance. DEER: two-toed cloven hoof, pointed front; dewclaws show in deep substrate or running. RABBIT: rear feet land ahead of front feet in characteristic bounding pattern. CANINE vs FELINE: dogs show claw marks; cats usually do not (retractile). PREDATOR SIGN: 5-toed prints, heel pad visible. SCAT: size, content, freshness indicates species and diet. Follow game trails downhill or downwind to water sources at dawn/dusk.
fishing techniques primitive: SET LINE: 6-12 baited hooks on 30m line, tie to stable anchor, check every dawn and dusk. BAIT PRIORITY: earthworms, grubs, grasshoppers, fish entrails. SPEAR FISHING: stand motionless in shallow clear water, account for refraction (aim below apparent fish position). WEIR TRAP: wicker or stone funnel angled upstream, fish enter and cannot exit. TIDAL POOLS at low tide: mussels, oysters, crabs, limpets. SHELLFISH SAFETY: never harvest bivalves during red tide — paralytic shellfish poisoning is fatal within hours.
medicinal plants field reference: YARROW (feathery leaves, white flat flower clusters): apply crushed leaves directly to wound — stops bleeding, antimicrobial. PLANTAIN (oval ribbed leaves everywhere): crush and apply as poultice — draws out thorns/venom, anti-inflammatory. WILLOW BARK: contains salicin (aspirin precursor) — steep inner bark in hot water for fever/pain. PINE: inner bark (cambium) eaten as emergency food; pitch for wound sealing and fire starting; needles make vitamin C tea. ELDER FLOWERS: diaphoretic for fever management. ALWAYS cross-reference identification before using any plant medicinally.
camp hygiene disease prevention: HANDWASHING: 20 seconds minimum with soap before food preparation and after latrine use. LATRINE: 60m minimum from any water source, downwind of camp, 20cm deep cat hole covered completely. FOOD STORAGE: 100m from sleeping area in bear country; hang at least 4m high, 1m from trunk. DISH WASHING: carry wash water 60m from water source before disposing. ONE CONTAMINATION EVENT can make entire group sick — protect water source with obsessive discipline. Boil all drinking water when pathogen status unknown.
rope making natural fibers: MATERIALS: stinging nettle (dry first), inner bark of basswood/linden/elm, dogbane/Indian hemp, cattail leaves, yucca leaves. REVERSE-TWIST METHOD: divide fibers into two equal bundles; twist each bundle clockwise independently; then twist both together counterclockwise while feeding in new fibers at staggered intervals for continuous length. 3-ply for load-bearing. STRENGTH TEST: hang full body weight before trusting life to any improvised cordage.
basic building cob and clay: COB MIX: 1 part clay, 2 parts sharp sand, chopped straw for tensile strength. STOMP with bare feet to combine until homogeneous. BUILD in 30cm lifts, allow each to stiffen 24-48h before adding next lift. WALLS: minimum 45cm thick for thermal mass and structural stability. WATTLE AND DAUB: woven branch framework (wattle) plastered with cob — faster than solid cob. ADOBE BRICKS: cob dried in molds in sun, stacked with mud mortar. FINISH: lime plaster protects exterior from rain.
fire management safety: FIRE RING: clear 3m radius of all combustibles; ring of rocks contains coals. EXTINGUISH: smother with dirt/sand first, then douse with water, stir until no steam — if soil is hot it is not out. WILDFIRE ESCAPE: move perpendicular to fire direction (never directly away — fire travels faster). UPHILL FIRE: moves faster than downhill (heated air rises). FIREBREAKS: roads, rivers, rocky outcrops, plowed strips. BUILD survival signal fire at clearing edge — light only when rescue is visible.
navigation terrain features: RIDGE: elongated high ground — follow to peaks or saddles. SPUR: high ground projecting from ridge — narrows as it descends, like a finger. DRAW: low ground between spurs — water collects here after rain. SADDLE: low point between two peaks — natural crossing point. DEPRESSION: closed low ground with no outflow. CLIFF: vertical face — tightly packed contour lines on map. RULE: ridges run down from peaks; valleys/draws run up to ridges. Follow water downstream in temperate regions — leads to human settlement.
tool maintenance field: KNIFE: sharpen on whetstone at 20-degree consistent angle per side, finish with leather strop. AXE: file to convex edge geometry, never use electric grinder (removes temper). SAW BLADE: alternate tooth set slightly left/right prevents binding, file each tooth same number of strokes. ALL METAL: coat lightly with oil or animal fat to prevent rust; wipe dry before use to prevent slipping. WOODEN HANDLES: treat with raw linseed oil, allow to fully dry. REPAIR HANDLES IMMEDIATELY — damaged tools cause injuries.
water from environment: MORNING DEW: drag cloth across grass at dawn, wring into container — 0.5-2L possible in good conditions. TRANSPIRATION BAG: clear plastic bag sealed over leafy branch in sunlight — 0.5-1L per day, change location every 2 days. DIG FOR SEEPAGE: outer bend of dry riverbeds, base of cliffs, low points of valleys — sand/gravel moisture zone. GREEN BAMBOO: cut internode at tilt — clear liquid collects. COASTAL: NEVER drink seawater — causes accelerated dehydration; distill using solar still or fire + catchment.
fermentation food safety: LACTO-FERMENTATION: Lactobacillus converts sugars to lactic acid, lowering pH below 4.5 — hostile to pathogens including Salmonella and E. coli. EQUIPMENT: only salt, vessel, and time required. BRINE RATIO: 2% salt by weight of vegetables for sauerkraut/kimchi. YOGURT: heat milk to 82C, cool to 43C, add 2 tbsp live culture, maintain 43C for 8h. SOURDOUGH STARTER: flour plus water, wild yeast capture from air, feed daily. DISCARD if: colored mold (not white), putrid smell (not sour), or slimy texture.
emergency calorie sources: INSECTS: 100g crickets = 120kcal + complete protein; 100g mealworms = 200kcal. All insects safe if cooked — kills parasites. Remove wings and legs first. PINE INNER BARK (cambium): starchy, edible raw or cooked, available year-round. CATTAIL: pollen (spring) = high-calorie flour substitute; green seed heads (summer) eaten like corn; rhizomes (year-round) = starch source like potato. ACORNS: leach tannins in running water or multiple water changes — then roast as flour or eat directly. DANDELION: entire plant edible — roots roasted make coffee substitute.
hunting primitive methods: SNARE placement: game trail, 30-45cm diameter loop, 25cm above ground (rabbit height), anchored to stake. DEADFALL (figure-four): notched sticks hold heavy flat rock, bait on trigger — triggers on any pressure. SPEAR: straight-grained hardwood, harden tip in coals (char, not burn), point at 45-degree angle. BOW: self-bow from yew/osage orange/black locust/ash, draw weight 25-40lbs for small game, 60lbs+ for deer. ETHICS AND LEGALITY: primitive trapping for genuine survival only; check all traps every 24h maximum; use the whole animal.
